name: tex-side-preview
description: Overleaf-style LaTeX in VS Code, Cursor and VSCodium: live PDF preview with SyncTeX, one-click compiler install, templates, citations from DOI/arXiv/Zotero, AI writing and review, comments and tracked changes, and two-way Overleaf sync.

commands.title: Open TeX Preview to the Side
Set API Key for OpenAI-compatible Endpoint…

texPreview.engine.description: Compiler to use. 'auto' picks the first available of latexmk, tectonic, pdflatex.

texPreview.outDir.description: Folder (relative to the root .tex file) for the PDF and auxiliary files. Use '.' to build next to the source.

texPreview.compileOnSave.description: Recompile whenever a .tex/.bib/.sty/.cls file is saved.

texPreview.extraPath.description: Extra directories to search for TeX binaries (added before the default macOS/Linux TeX locations).

texPreview.overleaf.autoSync.description: Two-way sync for folders cloned from Overleaf via Git: push on save, pull on a timer and when the window regains focus.

texPreview.overleaf.pullInterval.description: Seconds between checks for changes made on Overleaf.

texPreview.overleaf.pushDelay.description: Seconds to wait after a save before pushing, so quick successive saves go up as one commit.

texPreview.buildCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command that replaces the built-in build, e.g. `latexmk -pdf -outdir=%OUTDIR% %DOC%`. Placeholders: `%DOC%` (main file without extension), `%DOCFILE%` (its name), `%TEX%`, `%DIR%`, `%OUTDIR%`. The PDF is expected at `%OUTDIR%/%DOCFILE%.pdf`.

texPreview.docker.image.markdownDescription: Run the compiler inside this Docker image (e.g. `texlive/texlive`) instead of a local TeX install. The workspace folder is mounted at the same path.

enumDescriptions: Dark PDF when VS Code uses a dark theme.
texPreview.invertPdf.markdownDescription: Show the PDF with dark pages. The ◐ button in the preview toggles it for that preview.

texPreview.chktex.markdownDescription: Lint `.tex` files with [ChkTeX](https://www.nongnu.org/chktex/) as you type (needs `chktex`, included in TeX Live).

enumDescriptions: Yellow squiggles; files, outline and scrollbar are coloured yellow.
Blue squiggles and scrollbar marks; files and outline aren't coloured.
Faint dots only; hidden from the Problems panel and scrollbar.
texPreview.chktexSeverity.markdownDescription: How ChkTeX warnings are shown. ChkTeX errors are always shown as errors.

texPreview.spellcheck.enabled.markdownDescription: Check spelling in `.tex` files as you type, offline. Math, commands, labels, citations, comments and the preamble are skipped, as are author names from the project's `.bib` files.

texPreview.spellcheck.language.markdownDescription: Spelling dictionary: `en-US` or `en-GB` (bundled), a Hunspell name like `de_DE` installed in a standard Hunspell folder, or the path of a `.dic` file. A file can choose its own with `% !TeX spellcheck = en_GB` in its first lines. Grammar checks use the same language.

texPreview.spellcheck.words.markdownDescription: Words to accept. **Add to dictionary** quick fixes add them here, in user or workspace settings (both lists are used).

texPreview.grammar.enabled.markdownDescription: Check grammar and style with [LanguageTool](https://languagetool.org). **The prose of open files is sent to `#texPreview.grammar.server#`** (by default the public LanguageTool API, limited to 20 requests a minute). Run your own server for privacy and no limits, e.g. `docker run -p 8010:8010 erikvl87/languagetool` and set the server to `http://localhost:8010`.

texPreview.grammar.server.markdownDescription: LanguageTool server. With a Premium `#texPreview.grammar.username#` and API key (**TeX: Set LanguageTool Premium API Key…**), the public server switches to the Premium one.

texPreview.grammar.username.markdownDescription: LanguageTool Premium username (email), used with the API key.

texPreview.grammar.disabledRules.markdownDescription: LanguageTool rule IDs to ignore. The defaults are rules that misfire on LaTeX (spacing and quotes from markup, lowercase list items). **Disable grammar rule** quick fixes add to this list.

texPreview.externalViewer.command.markdownDescription: Command for **TeX: Open PDF in External Viewer**, e.g. `open -a Skim %PDF%`. Empty opens the system's default PDF app.

texPreview.externalViewer.syncCommand.markdownDescription: Forward search in the external viewer, used by **Jump to Location in PDF** when the PDF is open externally. Placeholders `%PDF%`, `%TEX%`, `%LINE%`, e.g. `/Applications/Skim.app/Contents/SharedSupport/displayline -r %LINE% %PDF% %TEX%`.

texPreview.review.author.markdownDescription: Your name on comments and tracked changes. Empty uses Git's `user.name`.

enumDescriptions: GitHub Copilot, or another extension's model, through VS Code's Language Model API.
The Claude Code CLI (`claude`), using your Claude subscription.
The Codex CLI (`codex`), using your ChatGPT plan.
Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, Groq, vLLM, OpenAI…
texPreview.ai.provider.markdownDescription: Where **Rewrite with AI**, **Write with AI** and **Fix with AI** send their requests: the passage, nearby text and the preamble's package and macro lines. **TeX AI: Choose AI Provider…** sets this up.

texPreview.ai.model.markdownDescription: Model to use. Copilot: a model id or family (empty lets Copilot choose). Claude / Codex: passed as `--model` / `-m` (empty uses the CLI's default). OpenAI-compatible: required, e.g. `llama3.1`; you're asked on first use.

texPreview.ai.baseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the part before `/chat/completions`). The API key, if needed, is kept in VS Code's secret storage: **TeX AI: Set API Key…**.

texPreview.ai.trackChanges.markdownDescription: Add AI edits as tracked changes you can accept or reject, even when Track Changes is off. Off: AI edits are plain edits (undo with Ctrl/Cmd+Z).

languageModelTools.name: texpreview_compile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Build the LaTeX project and report its errors and warnings.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles the LaTeX project that contains the given .tex file (saving its unsaved files first) with the user's configured compiler, and returns whether the build succeeded plus every error and warning with file and line. Use it after editing LaTeX to check the document still builds, and to find what to fix. Prefer it over running latexmk/pdflatex in a terminal: it uses the right main file, output folder and engine, and updates the user's PDF preview.

file.description: Path of any .tex file in the project (absolute, or relative to the workspace). Defaults to the active editor.

languageModelTools.name: texpreview_project
languageModelTools.userDescription: The project's main file, files, packages, macros, numbered outline, labels and bibliography keys.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Describes the LaTeX project that contains the given .tex file: its main file, the files pulled in with \input/\include, document class, packages, user macros, the numbered outline of sections with file:line, all \label names with file:line, and the bibliography entries (key, first author, year, title). Use it before writing \ref or \cite commands so labels and citation keys exist, and to find where a section lives.

file.description: Path of any .tex file in the project. Defaults to the active editor.

languageModelTools.name: texpreview_addReference
languageModelTools.userDescription: Fetch BibTeX for a DOI or arXiv id and add it to the project's .bib file.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches the BibTeX entry for a DOI (e.g. 10.1038/nature14539) or an arXiv id (e.g. 1706.03762) from doi.org or arxiv.org and adds it to the project's .bib file (creating references.bib if there is none), reusing an existing entry with the same DOI or arXiv id. Returns the citation key to use in \cite{}. Only use real identifiers you are sure of; never invent DOIs.

id.description: A DOI, an arXiv id, or a doi.org / arxiv.org URL.

file.description: Path of any .tex file in the project. Defaults to the active editor.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with LaTeX in VS Code
walkthroughs.description: From an empty folder to a live PDF in a minute: a compiler, a project, the preview, AI help and Overleaf.

steps.title: Get a LaTeX compiler
steps.description:
Builds need a TeX distribution (TeX Live, MacTeX, MiKTeX) or Tectonic. If you have none, install Tectonic with one click: about 20 MB, and it fetches the packages a document needs.
[Install Tectonic](command:texPreview.installTectonic)
[Check for a compiler](command:texPreview.checkCompiler)

steps.title: Start a project
steps.description:
Pick a template: article, thesis with chapters, Beamer slides, CV, homework, letter, IEEE or ACM paper. Or open a folder with your own .tex files.
[New LaTeX Project](command:texPreview.newProject)

media.altText: A LaTeX source on the left and its PDF on the right

steps.title: Open the live preview
steps.description:
Click the TeX button at the top right of a .tex file, or press ⌥⌘V (Ctrl+Alt+V). Save, and the PDF updates beside your source.
[Open Preview](command:texPreview.open)

media.altText: Live PDF preview beside the source

steps.title: Jump between source and PDF
steps.description:
Double-click a word in the PDF to jump to its source line. Press ⌥⌘J (Ctrl+Alt+J) in the source to highlight that line in the PDF.
[Jump to Location in PDF](command:texPreview.syncToPdf)

media.altText: A highlighted line in the PDF after jumping from the source

steps.title: Write faster
steps.description:
Paste a screenshot to add it as a figure, add citations from a DOI, arXiv id or Zotero, and get suggestions for \cite, \ref and commands as you type.
[Add Citation](command:texPreview.addCitation)

steps.title: Write and review with AI
steps.description:
Rewrite a paragraph, write LaTeX from a description, turn a photo of an equation into LaTeX, or get review comments, with Copilot, your Claude or ChatGPT plan, or a local model. Results arrive as tracked changes.
[Choose AI Provider](command:texPreview.ai.chooseProvider)

media.altText: An AI rewrite shown as a tracked change

steps.title: Work with Overleaf co-authors
steps.description:
Clone an Overleaf project and keep it in sync both ways: your saves are pushed, their changes are pulled. Comments and tracked changes travel with it.
[Clone Overleaf Project](command:texPreview.overleaf.clone)

media.altText: The Overleaf sync status in the status bar
